en: “tv” for “ttv” (as in *satva* etc.);
“nv” for “nnv” (as in *yanv ahaṃ* etc.).
The Ultimate Litany of Names of the Wisdom Being Mañjuśrī.
Homage to Mañjuśrī Kumārabhūta!
Now, the glorious Vajradhara, the supreme subduer of the difficult to tame,
the hero who conquers the three worlds, the king of secrets, the lord of the vajra.
His eyes are like blossomed white lotuses, his face is like a fully opened lotus,
and he repeatedly brandishes an excellent vajra with his own hand.
Accompanied by infinite Vajrapāṇis, foremost among whom are those with ripples of frowns—
heroes who subdue the difficult-to-tame, possessing forms that are both heroic and loathsome.
With their own hands brandishing the tips of flashing vajras,
they are supreme beings who accomplish the welfare of the world through wisdom, skillful means, and great compassion.

Together with the Protectors who perform the deeds of a Buddha, whose intentions are joyful and satisfied, who are gladdened, who manifest forms of wrathful bodies, and who stand with bodies bowed in prostration.
Having bowed to the Lord, the Perfectly Awakened One, the Blessed Tathāgata,
he stood before him with palms joined in reverence and spoke these words.
For my benefit, for my sake, and out of compassion for me, O Lord, [teach] so that I may become an attainer of the perfect awakening through the Net of Illusion. Mns 7.
For the benefit of all sentient beings who are submerged in the mire of ignorance and whose minds are agitated by the afflictions, and for the attainment of the unsurpassed fruit.

May the Perfectly Awakened One, the Blessed One, the Teacher, the Guru of the World— supreme knower of the reality of the great samaya, who understands the faculties and dispositions [of beings]— reveal it.
Of the Bhagavat’s wisdom-body, the Great Uṣṇīṣa, the Lord of Speech,
Mañjuśrī the Wisdom-being, the embodiment of wisdom, the Self-arisen One.
The supreme *Nāmasaṃgīti*, which possesses profound meaning, noble meaning, and great meaning; which is peerless, auspicious, and virtuous in its beginning, middle, and end.
That which has been spoken by the Buddhas of the past, will be spoken by those of the future,
and is spoken again and again by the Perfectly Awakened Ones of the present.
And that which is fully proclaimed in this *Māyājāla-mahātantra* by the immeasurable, joyful holders of mantra, the Great Vajradharas; Mns 13.
And I, with firm resolve, shall uphold this until final liberation,
so that I may become, O Protector, a bearer of the secrets of all the Buddhas.
I shall reveal [this] for the sake of sentient beings according to the distinctions of their inclinations,
for the destruction of all afflictions and for the abandonment of all ignorance.
Having thus entreated the Tathāgata, Vajrapāṇi, the Lord of Secrets,
stood before him with his body bowed low and his palms joined in reverence.
The sixteen verses of entreaty:
Then the Blessed One Śākyamuni, the Perfectly Awakened One, the supreme among bipeds,
extended his long, broad, and beautiful tongue from his own mouth.
Displaying a smile that purifies the three lower realms for all beings,
illuminates the three worlds, and subdues the enemy of the four Māras.
With a sweet, Brahma-like voice that filled the three worlds,
he addressed Vajrapāṇi, the lord of secrets and possessor of great power.
Excellent, O glorious Vajradhara! Excellent to you, O Vajrapāṇi, you who, endowed with great compassion, act for the benefit of the world.
You are prepared to hear from me the *Nāmasaṃgīti*, which is of great significance, purifying, and the destroyer of evil, belonging to Mañjuśrī, the Gnosis-Body.
"Therefore, O Lord of Guhyakas, I shall teach it well to you;
listen with a one-pointed mind. "Very well, Blessed One," he replied.
Then there are six verses of response;
thereafter, the Blessed One Śākyamuni, having surveyed the entire great mantra family, the family of mantra-vidyādharas, and the three families— *mansūtra 23*
The worldly and supramundane family, the great family that illuminates the world,
the supreme family of Mahāmudrā, and the great family of Mahoṣṇīṣa.
These two verses on the observation of the six families,
which are joined with these six mantra-kings, which give rise to non-duality,
and which possess the nature of non-arising— these were spoken by the Lord of Speech.
A Ā I Ī U Ū E AI O AU AṂ AḤ— abiding in the heart,
I am the embodiment of wisdom, the awakened one among all Buddhas who exist throughout the three times.
Oṃ, homage to you, the embodiment of the wisdom-knowledge that cuts through suffering with the vajra-sharp [blade], the Lord of Speech, the Knowledge-Body, Arapacana. Mns_27.
Three verses on the stages of awakening through the Net of Illusion (Māyājālābhisaṃbodhikrama).
That is to say: the Blessed One, the Buddha, the Perfectly Awakened One, is born from the syllable *A*;
the syllable *A* is the foremost of all phonemes, of great significance, and the supreme syllable.
For it is the Great Vital Breath, unborn, and devoid of verbal expression;
it is the foremost cause of all designations and is the perfect radiance of all speech.
The great festival of great passion, who brings delight to all sentient beings;
the great festival of great hatred, the great enemy of all afflictions.
The great festival, the great delusion, the destroyer of the delusion of the dull-witted;
the great festival, the great wrath, the great enemy of wrath, the Great One.
The great festival, the great greed, the destroyer of all greed;
the great desire, the great bliss, the great joy, and the great delight.
Possessing a great form, a great body, a great complexion, and a great physique;
great in name, great in magnificence, and possessing a vast and extensive mandala.
Wielding the great weapon of wisdom, the supreme goad against the great afflictions,
he possesses great renown, great fame, great radiance, and great splendor.
The wise one who possesses the great illusion, the accomplisher of the purpose of the great illusion,
who delights in the joy of the great illusion, and the master of the great illusory net.
The supreme great lord of giving, the foremost upholder of great ethical discipline,
the steadfast possessor of great patience, and one whose prowess is great vigor.
Abiding in the samādhi of great meditative concentration, he maintains the body of great wisdom;
he possesses great power and great skillful means, an ocean of the knowledge of his vows.
Consisting of great loving-kindness, immeasurable, possessing great compassion, supreme in intellect;
possessing great wisdom, of vast intelligence, possessing great skillful means, and of great creative power.
Endowed with the power of great supernatural faculties, possessing great impetus and great speed;
of great miraculous power, of great renown, and of great strength and prowess.
The shatterer of the great mountain of existence, the dense wielder of the great vajra;
the greatly fierce, the greatly terrible, the inspirer of fear in those who cause great fear.
The Lord is the supreme among great vidyās; the Guru is the supreme among great mantras.
He is established in the system of the Mahāyāna and is the highest of the Mahāyāna systems.
The fourteen verses on the great maṇḍala of the Vajradhātu.
Buddha Mahāvairocana, the great observer of silence, the great sage;
arisen from the Great Way of Mantra, he is the very essence of the Great Way of Mantra.
He has attained the ten perfections; he is the foundation of the ten perfections;
he is the purity of the ten perfections; he is the method of the ten perfections.
The Lord is the master of the ten stages, established upon the ten stages;
his self is purified by the ten knowledges, and he upholds the purity of the ten knowledges.
The Lord of Sages has ten aspects and ten purposes; he is the All-pervading One endowed with the ten powers.
He accomplishes the welfare of the entire universe without exception; he is the Great One who masters the ten aspects.
Free from mental anguish, his nature is beyond conceptual proliferation; he is of pure nature and has suchness as his essence.
He speaks of reality, speaks according to what is, acts accordingly, and his speech is never otherwise.
Non-dual and proponent of non-duality, established in the limit of reality;
with the lion’s roar of selflessness, he terrifies the deer-like false teachers.
All-pervading, of unfailing movement, with the speed of a Tathāgata’s mind;
the Victor, conqueror of enemies, triumphant, a universal monarch of great power.

The leader of the hosts, the teacher of the hosts, the lord of the hosts, the master of the hosts, the self-controlled one; he of great majesty, the foremost leader, not led by another, the one of the great path.
Lord of Speech, Master of Speech, eloquent, Lord of Words, of infinite voice;
speaker of truth, proclaimer of truth, and teacher of the Four Truths.
For he is irreversible, a non-returner, a rhinoceros-like solitary leader;
having emerged through various means of deliverance, he is the single cause of the great elements.
The Arhat, the monk whose taints are exhausted, free from passion, with senses conquered,
has attained peace, attained fearlessness, become cooled, and is indeed undisturbed.
Endowed with wisdom and conduct, the Sugata, the supreme knower of the world,
free from "mine-ness" and egoism, abides in the principle of the two truths.
Standing at the far shore of saṃsāra, he has accomplished what was to be done and stands on firm ground;
established in the knowledge of absolute liberation, he is the destroyer who wields the weapon of wisdom.
The True Dharma is the King of Dharma, radiant, the supreme illuminator of the world;
it is the Lord of Dharma, the King of Dharma, and the teacher of the path to excellence.
He whose purpose is accomplished and whose resolve is fulfilled is free from all conceptual constructs;
he is the non-conceptual, inexhaustible realm, the supreme and imperishable *dharmadhātu*.
He is meritorious, possessing the accumulation of merit; he is wisdom, the great source of wisdom;
he is possessed of wisdom, knowing the real and the unreal, and is fully endowed with the two accumulations.
Eternal, the sovereign of the universe, the yogi, meditation, the object of meditation, and the lord of intellects;
he is to be realized within oneself, immovable, the supreme primordial one, the sustainer of the three bodies.
The Buddha is the embodiment of the five bodies, the all-pervading lord whose nature is the five wisdoms;
he wears a crown consisting of the five Buddhas and possesses the five eyes that hold all without attachment.
The progenitor of all Buddhas, the supreme and most excellent son of the Buddha; born from the source of wisdom, unborn, the source of the Dharma, he brings an end to cyclic existence.
He is the solid essence, of the nature of a diamond, the newly born Lord of the World;
he is born from space, self-existent, the great fire of the wisdom of insight.
Vairocana of great brilliance, Virocana, the light of gnosis;
the lamp of the world, the torch of gnosis, of great splendor, and luminous.
King of Vidyās, supreme lord of mantras, king of mantras who accomplishes the great purpose;
Great Uṣṇīṣa, wondrous Uṣṇīṣa, beholder of all, lord of the sky.
The foremost embodiment of all Buddhas, whose eyes bring joy to the world,
the creator of manifold forms, the venerable and honorable great Ṛṣi.
The mantra-practitioner upholds the three families and maintains the mantra of the great samaya;
he is the supreme bearer of the Three Jewels and the teacher of the highest of the three vehicles.
Amoghapāśa, the victorious one; Vajrapāśa, the great seizer;
Vajrāṅkuśa, the great noose; Vajrabhairava, the terrifier.
The verses on the knowledge of the perfectly pure realm of phenomena (suviśuddhadharmadhātujñāna) consist of twenty-four and a quarter [verses].
The King of Wrath, six-faced and terrifying, with six eyes, six arms, and powerful;
a skeleton formidable with fangs, possessing hundreds of faces like the Halāhala poison.
Yamāntaka, Vighnarāj, Vajravega, Bhayaṃkara,
Vighuṣṭavajra, Hṛdvajra, Māyāvajra, and Mahodara.
Lord of the thunderbolt, born from the vajra, the vajra-mandala, like unto space;
possessing the majesty of a single immovable matted lock, he wears a moist garment of elephant hide.
The great and terrible cry of "hā hā," the fearsome sound of "hī hī," the loud laughter,
the great laughter, the diamond-like laugh, and the great roar.
Vajrasattva, the Great Being; Vajrarāja, the Great Bliss;
Vajracaṇḍa, the Great Joy; Vajrahūṃkāra, the Utterer of Hūṃ.
Wielding the weapon of the vajra-arrow, the vajra-sword that cuts through all,
the bearer of the universal vajra, the Vajrin, the sole Vajrin who abandons conflict.
His eyes are formidable with vajra-flames, and his hair is vajra-flames;
he is the vajra-penetration, the great penetration, the hundred-eyed one, and the vajra-eyed one.
His body consists of sprouts of vajra-hair; he possesses a singular form of vajra-hair;
he has the commencement of vajra-tips as his nails; and his skin is as dense as the essence of the vajra.
The glorious wearer of the vajra-garland, adorned with vajra ornaments,
whose roar is the loud laughter of "hā hā," the sound of the vajra, the six-syllabled one.
Mañjughoṣa, the great roar, the sole supreme one in the three worlds, his voice extends to the limits of the realm of space; he is the best among those possessed of voice.
The verses on the mirror-like wisdom (ādarśajñāna) consist of nine and three-quarter stanzas.
Suchness, true selflessness, the limit of reality, and the ineffable;
the bull among those who proclaim emptiness, whose roar is profound and vast.
The great-sounding conch of Dharma, the great drum of Dharma,
the nirvāṇa that is non-abiding, and the drum of Dharma resounding in the ten directions.
Formless yet possessing form, supreme, manifold in form, and made of mind;
he is the glory that illuminates all forms, bearing the reflections of everything without exception.
Invincible, of great renown, the Great Lord of the three realms;
established upon the exalted Noble Path, the Banner of Dharma, of vast success.
The body of the sole youth of the three worlds, he is the ancient, aged Lord of Creatures;
bearing the thirty-two marks, he is lovely and the most beautiful in the three worlds.
The Teacher of the qualities of worldly knowledge, the Teacher of the world, the fearless one;
the Protector, the Savior, the Friend of the three worlds, the Refuge, the Deliverer, the unsurpassed.
Enjoying the vast expanse of space, he is an ocean of omniscient wisdom;
he shatters the shell of the egg of ignorance and rends asunder the cage of existence.
Having pacified all afflictions, he has reached the further shore of the ocean of saṃsāra;
crowned with the consecration of primordial wisdom, he is adorned as a perfectly awakened Buddha.
The pacifier of the suffering of the three types of suffering, the one who has reached the end, the infinite, the one who has attained the three liberations;
liberated from all obscurations, he has attained equality with space.
Transcending the stains of all afflictions, he has reached the state beyond the path of the three times;
he is the great elephant among all beings, the crest-jewel upon the crests of all virtues.
Completely liberated from all substrates of existence, firmly established on the path of space,
the Lord is the bearer of the great wish-fulfilling gem, the supreme among all jewels.
He is the vast and flourishing great wish-fulfilling tree, the supreme and magnificent vase of excellence;
he is the performer of the welfare of all sentient beings, the benefactor who seeks their well-being and is compassionate toward them.
He knows the auspicious and the inauspicious; he knows the time, he knows the occasion, and he is the pervasive master who observes the commitments.
He knows the faculties of sentient beings, he knows the proper moment, and he is skilled in the three liberations.
He is the possessor of virtues, the knower of virtues, the knower of Dharma, the praised one, the source of auspiciousness;
he is the most auspicious among all auspicious things, fame, fortune, glory, and goodness.
The great festival, the great relief, the great bliss, the great delight;
honor, veneration, prosperity, joy, glory, and the lord of fame.
The one to be chosen, the giver of boons, the most excellent, the worthy refuge, the supreme shelter,
the enemy of great fear, the preeminent one, the destroyer of all fears without exception.
He has a crest, he wears a topknot, he has matted hair, he is shaggy-haired, he is shaven-headed, and he wears a diadem;
he is five-faced, he has five tufts of hair, and his crest is adorned with five locks of hair.
Wearing the great vows, girded with a muñja-grass belt, a celibate student, supreme in his observances,
a great ascetic devoted to austerity, a bath-graduate, Gautama was the leader.
The knower of Brahman is the Brāhmaṇa; he is Brahmā, who has attained the nirvāṇa of Brahman. He is liberation, release, the limb of liberation, emancipation, tranquility, and auspiciousness.
Nirvāṇa, cessation, peace, the supreme good, the exit, the end; the maker of an end to pleasure and pain, the ultimate goal, dispassion, and the exhaustion of the substrates of existence.
Unconquered, incomparable, unmanifest, without appearance,
stainless, partless, all-pervading, omnipresent, subtle, the seed, and untainted.
Free from dust, stainless, immaculate, with faults cast out and free from affliction;
perfectly awakened, one whose self is fully enlightened, the omniscient, the all-knowing, the supreme.
Transcending the nature of consciousness, wisdom maintains a non-dual form;
it is free from conceptual construction, effortless, and performs the enlightened activities of the Buddhas of the three times.
The Buddha is without beginning or end, the primordial Buddha, free from lineage;
he is the stainless eye of singular gnosis, the embodiment of gnosis, the Tathāgata.
Lord of Speech, great debater, king of speakers, bull among disputants;
the best of those who speak, the most excellent, lion of speakers, unconquered.
Samantadarśin, Prāmodya, Tejomālī, Sudarśana,
Śrīvatsa, Suprabha, Dīpti, Bhā, and Bhāsurakaradyuti.
The supreme and most excellent great physician, the peerless remover of thorns;
the tree of all medicines without exception, the great enemy of the disease of the afflictions.
The beloved Tilaka of the three worlds, glorious, the circle of the stars,
extending to the limits of the sky in the ten directions, he is the great, lofty banner of Dharma.
The sole vast umbrella of the world, the mandala of loving-kindness and compassion,
the glorious Padmanarteśvara, the great sovereign Ratnacchatra.
The great king of all Buddhas, who sustains the embodiment of all Buddhas;
the great yoga of all Buddhas, the sole teaching of all Buddhas.
The glory of the vajra-jewel initiation, the sovereign lord of all jewels,
the lord of the lords of all worlds, the supreme master of all vajra-holders.
The great mind of all Buddhas, the movement of the minds of all Buddhas,
the great body of all Buddhas, and the Sarasvatī of all Buddhas.
The Vajra-Sun, the great illumination, possessing the stainless radiance of the Vajra-Moon;
the Great Passion beginning with dispassion, blazing with light of every color.
The Perfectly Awakened One, seated in the vajra posture, who upholds the Dharma of the Buddhas' assembly;
the glorious one born from the lotus of the Buddha, who holds the treasury of omniscient wisdom.
The King who wields the universal illusion, the great master of the Buddhas' vidyā;
the Vajra-Sharp, the Great Sword, the utterly pure, the supreme syllable.
The Great Vehicle that cuts through suffering, the great weapon of Vajra-Dharma;
the Conqueror of conquerors, profound as a vajra, possessing vajra-intelligence, the knower of things as they truly are.
The fulfiller of all perfections, the ornament of all stages,
possessing the purity of the selflessness of phenomena, with the light of the moon of perfect gnosis radiating from his heart.
The great exertion of the *Māyājāla*, the supreme sovereign of all tantras;
he who sits in the vajra-posture without exception, and who sustains the body of omniscient gnosis.
Samantabhadra, the one of excellent intelligence, Kṣitigarbha, the sustainer of the world,
the great womb of all Buddhas, and the bearer of the wheel of manifold emanations.
Supreme essence of the nature of all phenomena, sustainer of the nature of all phenomena;
whose dharma is non-arising, the purpose of the universe, the sustainer of the nature of all dharmas.

Possessing great wisdom in a single instant, you uphold the realization of all phenomena; you are the direct comprehension of all dharmas, the Sage who has reached the limit of reality, endowed with supreme intelligence.
Stable, with a perfectly serene mind, he upholds the awakening of the Samyaksambuddhas;
he is manifest before all Buddhas, a flame of wisdom, most brilliantly radiant.
The forty-two verses on the wisdom of discernment:
He who accomplishes the desired aim, the supreme one, the purifier of all miserable states;
the protector, the highest among all beings, the liberator of all beings.
The sole hero in the battle against the afflictions, who destroys the pride of the enemy of ignorance;
he is Intelligence personified, bearing the sentiment of love, glorious, and assuming both heroic and loathsome forms.
He casts forth hundreds of staff-like arms; he dances with every step he takes;
possessing the magnificent expanse of a hundred arms, he dances across the vast expanse of the sky.
He stands with the surface of the earth’s mandala pressed by the sole of one foot,
and with the tip of the big toe and its nail resting upon the summit of the universe.
The single meaning is the meaning of the non-dual Dharma; it is the ultimate reality, indestructible.
The object of various representations and forms is the continuum of mind and consciousness.
Delighting in the meaning of all phenomena without exception, he delights in emptiness and possesses supreme wisdom;
transcending passion for existence and the like, he finds great delight in the three realms of existence.
White as a pure, bright cloud, with a radiance like the rays of the autumn moon;
possessing the luster of the orb of the rising sun, and the glow of great red nails.
With a sublime crest like the peak of an indranīla gem, bearing hair-tips as deep blue as a great sapphire,
possessing the splendor of the radiance of great jewels, he is adorned with the emanations of the Buddhas.
He causes a hundred world-systems to tremble; he possesses the great stride of the bases of miraculous power;
he is the bearer of great mindfulness, the reality itself, and the sovereign of the fourfold mindfulness and meditative concentration.
He is the fragrance of the flowers of the factors of enlightenment, an ocean of the qualities of the Tathāgatas;
he knows the method of the eightfold path and knows the path of perfect awakening.
He has great attachment for all sentient beings, yet he is free from attachment, like the sky;
he is born from the minds of all sentient beings and possesses the speed of the minds of all sentient beings.
He who knows the faculties and objects of all sentient beings, who captivates the minds of all sentient beings;
he who knows the reality of the meaning of the five aggregates, and who maintains the purity of the five aggregates.
Abiding at the pinnacle of all deliverance, skilled in all means of deliverance;
established on the path of all deliverance, the teacher of all deliverance.
He has uprooted existence with its twelve links, maintains the purity of the twelve aspects,
possesses the form of the method of the four truths, and maintains the realization of the eightfold knowledge.
He whose meaning of the truths consists of twelve aspects, who knows reality in sixteen aspects,
and whose awakening consists of twenty aspects— he is the fully awakened one, the supreme omniscient one.
He manifests millions of emanation bodies of immeasurable Buddhas;
he is the realization of all moments and knows the meaning of every moment of mind.
He manifests the welfare of the world through the various methods and means of the diverse vehicles;
having emerged from the three vehicles, he abides in the fruit of the single vehicle.
His self is purified of the realm of afflictions; he brings about the exhaustion of the realm of karma;
he has crossed over the ocean of the floods and emerged from the wilderness of yoga.
Having thoroughly abandoned the afflictions, secondary afflictions, and all defilements along with their latent tendencies,
he accomplishes the welfare of the world through wisdom, skillful means, and great compassion, never in vain.
The meaning of the abandonment of all perceptions, the meaning of consciousness, the upholder of cessation;
the object of the minds of all sentient beings, and the movement of the minds of all sentient beings.
Abiding within the minds of all sentient beings, having attained equality with their minds,
he gladdens the minds of all sentient beings and delights the minds of all sentient beings.
The established doctrine is free from delusion and devoid of all error;
it possesses a mind beyond doubt, has three meanings, encompasses all objects, and consists of the three qualities.
The meaning of the five aggregates, existing in the three times, he who discerns every moment,
perfectly awakened in a single instant, the upholder of the essential nature of all Buddhas.
Bodyless body, supreme body, the one who reveals the pinnacle of bodies;
he displays all forms without exception, the Jewel Banner, the Great Gem.
The twenty-four verses on the Wisdom of Equality:
"The unsurpassed enlightenment of all Buddhas is that which is to be realized by all Buddhas;
it is without syllables, the source of mantras, and the great mantra of the three families."
The great bindu, which gives rise to the meaning of all mantras, is without syllables;
it is the five-syllabled great void, the void of the bindu, and the hundred-syllabled one.
Possessing all forms yet formless, holding the sixteen, the eight, and the four drops;
partless and beyond calculation, he holds the pinnacle of the fourth dhyāna.
He is the master of all meditative arts, the knower of the lineage and family of samādhis;
he is the body of samādhi, the supreme body, and the sovereign of all enjoyment-bodies.
The Emanation Body is the supreme body, upholding the lineage of the Buddha’s emanations;
manifesting in diverse forms throughout the ten directions, it accomplishes the welfare of the world according to its needs.
The god beyond gods, the lord of gods, the sovereign of the Suras, the ruler of the Dānavas, the lord of the immortals, the preceptor of the gods, the destroyer, and the lord of the Pramathas.
Having crossed the wilderness of existence, he alone is the Teacher, the Guru of the world,
renowned throughout the worlds of the ten directions as the great Lord of the Gift of Dharma.
Girt with the armor of loving-kindness, clad in the mail of compassion,
and armed with the sword, bow, and arrows of wisdom, he abandons the battle against afflictions and ignorance.
The enemy of Māra, the conqueror of Māra, the hero who brings an end to the fear of the four Māras,
the vanquisher of all the hosts of Māra, the perfectly awakened one, the leader of the world.
He is to be venerated, worshipped, saluted, and honored perpetually;
he is the most worthy of adoration, the one to be revered, the one to be bowed to—the supreme Guru.
He whose stride traverses the three worlds alone, whose prowess extends to the limits of space,
who possesses the three types of knowledge, who is learned in the Vedas, who is purified, who has the six superknowledges, and who possesses the six recollections.
The Bodhisattva Mahāsattva has transcended the world and possesses great supernatural power;
established in the perfection of wisdom, he has attained the very nature of wisdom.
He knows himself and knows others; he is all, for he is the most excellent person.
Having transcended all comparisons, he is to be known as the supreme Lord of Wisdom.

The lord of the gift of Dharma is supreme, the teacher of the meaning of the four mudrās; he is most worthy of being attended by the worlds of those who proceed by way of the three vehicles of liberation.
The glorious one, pure in the ultimate sense; the great one, auspicious to the three worlds;
the bringer of all prosperity; the illustrious Mañjuśrī, the best among the glorious.
Fifteen verses on the knowledge of the performance of duties:
Homage to you, the bestower of boons, O foremost of Vajras; homage be to you, the limit of reality! Homage to you, whose womb is emptiness; homage be to you, the awakening of the Buddhas! Mns 158.
O Buddha-passion, homage be to you; O Buddha-desire, salutation after salutation.
O Buddha-joy, homage to you; O Buddha-delight, salutation after salutation.
Homage to you, Buddha-smile; homage again and again to the Buddha-laughter.
Homage be to you, O Buddha-voice; homage again and again to the Buddha-nature.
Homage be to you, O source of non-existence; homage to you, O source of the Buddha.
Homage to you, O source of space; homage to you, O source of primordial wisdom.
Homage to you, O Net of Illusion; homage to you, the Buddha’s drama;
homage to you, all of them; homage be to you, the body of gnosis.
Thus end the five verses of praise to the wisdoms of the five Tathāgatas.
This, O Vajrapāṇi, O Vajradhara, is the unique and completely pure *Nāmasaṃgīti* of the Blessed One Mañjuśrī-jñānasattva, who is the embodiment of wisdom and the wisdom-body of all Tathāgatas;
it is for the purpose of generating in you unsurpassed joy, serene faith, and great exultation, and for the complete purification of the secrets of body, speech, and mind.
For the sake of fulfilling and purifying the incomplete and impure accumulations of merit and wisdom pertaining to the stages and perfections;
for the realization of the unsurpassed goal not yet realized;
and for the attainment of what has not yet been attained.

"Furthermore, Vajrapāṇi, O Vajradhara, for the sake of upholding the guidance of the True Dharma of all Tathāgatas, this has been taught, fully revealed, explained, analyzed, clarified, and empowered by me within your own continuum through the empowerment of the reality-nature of all mantras."
Furthermore, Vajrapāṇi, O Vajradhara, this *Nāmasaṃgīti* is the secret of the body, speech, and mind of the perfectly pure and completely refined omniscient wisdom-body;
it is the awakening of all Tathāgatas and the realization of the perfectly awakened Buddhas.
It is the unsurpassed state of all Tathāgatas; it is the realization of the realm of phenomena (dharmadhātu) for all Sugatas;
it is the defeat of the power of all Māras for the Victors (Jinas).
It is the possession of the power of the ten powers among all those who possess the ten powers;
it is omniscience among all forms of knowledge;
it is the source of all the qualities of a Buddha.
It is the realization of all Buddhas;
it is the fulfillment of the accumulations of stainless and perfectly pure merit and wisdom for all great Bodhisattvas;
and it is the source of birth for all Śrāvakas and Pratyekabuddhas.
It is the field for the excellence of all gods and humans;
it is the foundation of the Mahāyāna;
it is the source of the conduct of Bodhisattvas.
It is the culmination of the noble path,
the touchstone of the liberations,
and the source of the path of deliverance.
The non-interruption of the lineage of the Tathāgatas; the increase of the family and clan of the great Bodhisattvas;
and the subduing of all rival proponents.
The destruction of all non-Buddhist teachers;
the defeat of the armies and forces of the four Māras;
and the gathering together of all sentient beings.
The maturation of the noble path for all those traveling toward liberation;
meditative concentration for those dwelling in the four divine abodes;
and dhyāna for those whose minds are one-pointed.
Yoga is the application of body, speech, and mind;
disjunction is the separation from all fetters;
abandonment is the relinquishing of all afflictions and secondary afflictions.
It is the pacification of all obscurations,
the liberation from all bonds,
and the release from all substrates of existence.
It is the pacification of all mental disturbances,
the source of all prosperities,
and the abandonment of all calamities.
It is the closing of all doors to the lower realms,
the true path to the city of liberation,
and the cessation of the wheel of saṃsāra.
The turning of the wheel of Dharma;
the raising of the parasols, banners, and flags of the Tathāgata’s teaching;
and the empowerment of the proclamation of all Dharmas.
Swift accomplishment belongs to those bodhisattvas who practice the conduct of the mantra-vehicle;
the attainment through cultivation belongs to those devoted to the perfection of wisdom;
and the penetration of emptiness belongs to those devoted to the cultivation of the penetration of non-duality.
It is the accomplishment of the equipment for all the perfections;
it is the complete purification for the fulfillment of the perfections on all the stages.
Penetration is the correct penetration of the four noble truths;
the penetration of all phenomena within a single mind is that of the four applications of mindfulness.
This *Nāmasaṃgīti* extends until the complete perfection of all the qualities of a Buddha.
This is the praise of the second wheel; its constituent phrases number fifty-two.
Furthermore, Vajrapāṇi, O Vajradhara, this *Nāmasaṃgīti* pacifies all misdeeds arising from the physical, verbal, and mental conduct of all sentient beings without exception;
it purifies all the miserable states of all sentient beings and wards off all rebirths in evil destinies.
It completely cuts through all karmic obscurations;
it prevents the arising of all eight inopportune births;
and it pacifies the eight great fears.
It destroys all bad dreams,
dispels all ill omens,
and pacifies all ill-omened portents and obstacles.
It brings about the distancing of all the activities of the enemy Māra;
it effects the accumulation of all roots of merit and virtue;
and it prevents the arising of all improper mental attention.
It is that which destroys all intoxication, pride, arrogance, and egoism;
it is that which prevents the arising of all suffering and mental distress;
and it is the very heart of all Tathāgatas.
It is the secret of all bodhisattvas,
the esoteric mystery of all śrāvakas and pratyekabuddhas,
and the essence of all mudrās and mantras.
It generates mindfulness and clear comprehension for those who proclaim that all phenomena are ineffable; it produces unsurpassed wisdom and intelligence;
and it brings about the perfection of health, strength, and sovereignty.
She who causes the increase of glory, auspiciousness, peace, and well-being;
she who brings forth the manifestation of fame, renown, celebrity, and praise;
she who pacifies all diseases and great fears.
The most purified of the purified, the most purifying of the purifying, the most auspicious of the auspicious.
The most auspicious of all that is most auspicious;
a refuge for those seeking refuge; a shelter for those seeking shelter.
A protection for those seeking protection;
a final resort for those without a resort;
an island for those seeking an island.
She has become the unsurpassed refuge for those who have no other resort; she has become a vessel of transport for those seeking to cross to the further shore of the ocean of existence;
and she has become a great king of medicines for the eradication of all diseases.
She is become wisdom for the sake of discerning what is to be abandoned and what is to be adopted;
she is become the light of knowledge for the sake of removing all darkness of ignorance and false views;
she is become a wish-fulfilling gem for the sake of fulfilling the intentions and aspirations of all sentient beings according to their inclinations.

It is the embodiment of the wisdom of the omniscient one, for the sake of attaining the wisdom-body of Mañjuśrī; it is the embodiment of pure knowledge and vision, for the sake of attaining the five eyes;
and it is the embodiment of the fulfillment of the six perfections, through the relinquishing of the gift of material goods, the gift of fearlessness, and the gift of the Dharma.
It is the attainment of the ten stages through the fulfillment of the equipment of merit, knowledge, and meditative concentration;
it is the non-dual nature of phenomena because it is free from dualistic phenomena.
It is the nature of suchness because it is free from the superimposition of other phenomena;
it is the nature of the limit of reality because its essence is the perfectly pure body of the Tathāgata’s gnosis;
and it is the nature of the great emptiness of all aspects because it eradicates the dense thicket of all erroneous views without exception.
This *Nāmasaṃgīti* has the ineffable nature of all phenomena; that is to say, it is for the purpose of revealing the non-dual reality by means of upholding the names.
This is the praise of the third wheel; its constituent phrases are fifty-two.
Furthermore, Vajrapāṇi, O Vajradhara, whatever son of noble family or daughter of noble family practices the conduct of the mantra-path,

[should recite] this *Nāmasaṃgīti*— the crest-jewel of names, which is the non-dual ultimate reality of the Blessed One Mañjuśrī-Jñānasattva, the wisdom-body of all Tathāgatas, the embodiment of wisdom— in its entirety, complete, without omission, and without defect, using these very same verses, phrases, and syllables.
Every day, without interruption, they will uphold, recite, master, and properly attend to it three times a day;
and for others, they will extensively expound it according to the occasion and according to what is appropriate, even down to clarifying the meaning of each individual name.
Taking the Mañjuśrī-jñānakāya as their object of focus, they will cultivate it with a one-pointed mind.

Dwelling in the Samantamukha abode through both resolute conviction and mental attention toward reality, he is endowed with a supreme, unclouded faith permeated by wisdom that penetrates all phenomena; for him, who is thus connected to the three times and the timeless,
all the Buddhas and Bodhisattvas will repeatedly assemble and manifest all the gateways to the Dharma.
And he will manifest his own physical form;

and the Great Kings of Wrath, such as Mahāvajradhara and others, who are the tamers of the difficult-to-tame and have become the protectors of the world, will manifest their vital energy, strength, splendor, and invincibility through various emanated form-bodies, and will display all the mudrās, mantras, realizations, and maṇḍalas.

And all the mantra-kings and queen-mantras, along with all the Vighnas, Vināyakas, Māras, Aris, Mahāpratyāṅgirās, and Mahāparājitās, will provide protection, shelter, and defense day and night, at every moment and in all modes of conduct;
they will also bestow the empowerment of all Buddhas and Bodhisattvas.
With their entire body, speech, and mind, they will correctly empower his mental continuum;
through the favor of all Buddhas and Bodhisattvas, they will bestow their grace upon him,
and they will provide him with the eloquence of fearlessness regarding all phenomena.
Out of a disposition of love for the noble Dharma of all Arhats, Śrāvakas, and Pratyekabuddhas, they will manifest their own bodies;
and those who are the world-protectors of the ten directions— Brahmā, Indra, Upendra, Rudra, Nārāyaṇa, Sanatkumāra, Maheśvara, Kārtikeya, Mahākāla, Nandikeśvara, Yama, Varuṇa, Kuvera, and Hārītī—
will [protect them] constantly and continuously, day and night, whether they are walking, standing, lying down, sitting, or sleeping.

Whether he is awake or asleep, composed or uncomposed, alone or in the midst of a great multitude; whether he is situated in the midst of villages, towns, market towns, districts, kingdoms, or royal capitals; whether he is in the middle of a gate-pivot, a carriage road, a main street, a city gate, a lane, a crossroads, a square, or a marketplace shop; or even when he has gone to an empty house, a mountain cave, a river, or a dense forest—whether he is defiled by food remnants or free from them, or even when he is intoxicated.
They will provide supreme protection, defense, and guardianship for one who is heedless at all times, in every way, and by every means;
they will provide supreme auspiciousness day and night.
And as for others—be they gods, nāgas, yakṣas, gandharvas, asuras, garuḍas, kinnaras, mahoragas, humans, non-humans, or any others—[they shall likewise do so].

The lords of the planets, constellations, and the hosts of mothers, as well as the seven mothers, and those who are yakṣiṇīs, rākṣasīs, and piśācīs— all of them together, complete, with their armies and retinues— will provide protection, defense, and guardianship; furthermore,
they will infuse vitality and strength into his body.
They will bestow health, strength, and an increase in lifespan.
This is the benefit of the fourth wheel; its phrases number nineteen.
Furthermore, Vajrapāṇi, O Vajradhara, whoever shall daily recite this *Nāmasaṃgīti*, the crest-jewel of names, three times with unbroken commitment until it is committed to memory;
or who, reading it from a book, shall cause it to proceed;
while taking as his object the form of the Blessed Lord Mañjuśrī-Jñānasattva, reflecting upon it and meditating on that very form.
Relying upon this very Dharma and Vinaya, he will soon behold that [Buddha] in his form-body (rūpakāya);
he will also behold all the Buddhas and Bodhisattvas situated in the expanse of the sky, accompanied by various manifested form-bodies.
That Mahāsattva shall never, at any time, or in any way, fall into the miserable states or the lower realms.
One will not be born into a low family;
one will not be born in a border region;
and one will not have impaired faculties.
He will not have impaired faculties;
he will not be born into a family with wrong views;
and he will not be reborn in buddha-fields where no Buddha resides.
There shall be no turning away from or lack of proximity to the arising of a Buddha and the Dharma taught by him; nor shall one be reborn among the long-lived gods;
nor shall one be reborn during the intermediate kalpas of famine, disease, and weapons.
Furthermore, one will not be reborn during the times of the five corruptions;
there will be no fear of kings, enemies, or thieves; and there will be no fear of poverty or any form of deficiency.
Furthermore, there will be no fear of ill-repute, slander, blame, infamy, or dishonor;
he will be endowed with a noble birth, lineage, and clan;
and he will be possessed of a form and complexion that is entirely serene and pleasing.
He will be dear to the world, pleasing, pleasant to dwell with, and lovely to behold;
he will possess beauty, good fortune, and speech that is persuasive to sentient beings.
Wherever he is reborn, in every birth he will be one who remembers his past lives.
He will possess great wealth and a great retinue; his enjoyments will be inexhaustible and his followers inexhaustible.
He will become a leader among all sentient beings, endowed with the foremost qualities, and by nature he will be endowed with the virtues of the six perfections.
He will dwell in the four divine abodes;
he will be endowed with mindfulness, clear comprehension, skillful means, power, aspiration, and knowledge;
and he will be skilled in all treatises and eloquent in speech.
He will possess clear speech, an unclouded and sharp intellect;
he will be skillful, diligent, contented, highly purposeful, and free from craving;
and he will be the object of supreme trust for all sentient beings.
He will be esteemed by his teachers, preceptors, and gurus;
and even those treatises on arts, crafts, supernormal knowledges, and sciences that he has never heard before will appear to him in their meaning and their textual form.
He will practice with a conduct of perfectly pure morality and livelihood; he will be one who has gone forth well and received full ordination well;
and he will never lose the great mind of awakening directed toward omniscience.
He shall never enter the fixed course of the disciples, arhats, or pratyekabuddhas.
This is the praise of the fifth wheel; its constituent phrases number fifty-one.
Thus, Vajrapāṇi, O Vajradhara, that person who practices the conduct of the mantra gateway will be endowed with immeasurable qualities;
he will be endowed with other immeasurable qualities of such a kind and such a nature.
Very soon, Vajrapāṇi, O Vajradhara, that bull among men who upholds the *Paramārthanāmasaṃgīti* will have well-accumulated the equipment of merit and wisdom.
Having more swiftly perfected the qualities of a Buddha, he will realize unexcelled, perfect enlightenment.

Possessing the dharma of no small parinirvāṇa, he is the teacher of the unexcelled dharma for all sentient beings; empowered as the King of Dharma, he is the drum of the true dharma in the ten directions.
These are the benefits of the sixth wheel, whose verses are immeasurable.

Oṃ! Vajra of the purity of the intrinsic nature of the non-existence of all phenomena: a ā aṃ aḥ! All phenomena are pure by nature, because they partake in the purity of Mañjuśrī, the wisdom-body of all Tathāgatas. A āḥ! Heart of all Tathāgatas! Seize, seize! Oṃ hūṃ hrīḥ! Blessed One, embodiment of wisdom, Lord of Speech, Great Voice, Womb of the Wisdom of the Dharmadhātu, which is perfectly pure and stainless like the sky of all phenomena! Āḥ!
The arrangement of the mantra.
Then the glorious Vajradhara, joyful and satisfied, with palms joined in reverence,
bowed down to the Lord, the Perfectly Awakened One, the Blessed Tathāgata.
Together with many other lords, the Indras of Secrets who hold the vajra,
and the kings of wrath, he spoke these words aloud:
We rejoice, O Protector; excellent, excellent is this well-spoken word!
A great benefit has been wrought for us, leading to the attainment of perfect enlightenment.
And for the world which is without a protector and yearns for the fruit of liberation,
this pure path to the highest good has been proclaimed through the method of the *Māyājāla*.
Profound, vast, and extensive, of great significance and accomplishing the welfare of the world—
this is indeed the domain of the Buddhas, taught by the Perfectly Enlightened Ones.
Thus are the five summary verses.

Thus concludes the *Paramārthanāmasaṃgīti* of the Blessed Mañjuśrī-jñānasattva, spoken by the Blessed Tathāgata Śākyamuni from the *Samādhijālapaṭala* within the *Mahāyogatantra* of sixteen thousand [verses] from the *Āryamāyājāla*.
